overview: Root cause: The application has no WebFinger endpoint (/.well-known/webfinger returns 404) and the /.well-known/change-password redirect is stranded inside the user route module instead of a dedicated .well-known router. The fix requires creating two new files — src/controllers/well-known.js (webfinger handler with resource validation, privilege gate, user resolution, and JSON response construction) and src/routes/well-known.js (route configuration module owning both .well-known routes) — then wiring them into the existing controller and route registries, and removing the now-orphaned inline redirect from src/routes/user.js. All changes follow established repo conventions: bracket-key controller registration (Controllers['404'] pattern), _mounts object composition + addCoreRoutes invocation pattern, and privileges.global.can for the view:users gate.

It exports a `webfinger` async function that: (1) validates the `resource` query param (missing → 400, no `acct:` prefix → 400, wrong hostname suffix using nconf.get('url_parsed').hostname → 400), (2) gates access with privileges.global.can('view:users', req.uid || 0) — passing 0 for unauthenticated callers routes through helpers.js:73 to the Guest role automatically — returning 403 on denial, (3) resolves the username slug to a UID returning 404 if not found, and (4) returns res.json({ subject, aliases: [uid-url, slug-url], links: [{ href: /user/<slug> }] }) on success. The module.exports.webfinger named-export style follows src/controllers/osd.js.
